seoTitle: How to Get the Outlook QR Code for Mobile Sign-In
metaDescription: Find the QR code in Outlook on the web to add your phone's Outlook Mobile app without typing a password, and why it may not appear at all on a work account.
intro:
Typing a long password on a phone keyboard is tedious, and Outlook has a shortcut for it: open Settings in Outlook on the web, and a temporary code appears that the Outlook mobile app can scan to add the account without you typing anything on a small screen.

This guide covers the actual settings path and what the code does. It also covers a constraint most write-ups skip: Microsoft paused this feature for work and school accounts in 2024, so depending on which kind of account you use, the option may not be there at all.
prerequisites: The Outlook mobile app installed on the Android or iPhone you want to pair

steps.heading: Sign in at Outlook.com
steps.body: Everything starts from the Outlook web landing page, which shows "Welcome to Microsoft Outlook" and a Sign in button before any mail loads. Use the Microsoft account you want your phone linked to, personal or work — the code that appears later pairs with whichever account is signed in at the time.

image.caption: The Outlook.com landing page before signing in. Pairing has to happen from the account you actually want your phone linked to.

steps.heading: Confirm you're in the right inbox
steps.body: Once signed in, you land in your inbox with the Focused and Other tabs across the top and the folder list down the left side. Check the account name in that folder pane before going further, especially if you keep more than one Outlook account open in the same browser — the account switcher makes it easy to generate a code for the wrong one.

image.caption: A signed-in Outlook web inbox, with the account name visible in the folder pane on the left — worth checking before pairing a device.

steps.heading: Open Settings
steps.body: Mobile options live behind the gear icon, which opens a Settings panel: a category list on the left — Account, General, Mail, Calendar, People — and a detail pane on the right. This is the same panel used for display and layout preferences, so the layout will already look familiar if you've changed message density or the reading pane before.

image.caption: The Settings panel, here showing the Mail > Layout screen. Account and mobile-related options sit in the same panel, under the Accounts category.

steps.heading: Open Accounts, then Mobile devices
steps.body: Click into Accounts and you land on your account details and any Microsoft subscription tied to that sign-in first. Mobile devices sits as its own item further down the same Accounts category; open it and select Get the Outlook app to bring up the code. If Accounts doesn't show a Mobile devices option at all, that's most likely the work-account restriction covered below, not a bug in your account.

image.caption: The Account details screen inside Settings, showing the signed-in address and subscription status. Mobile devices is listed further down the same Accounts category.

steps.heading: Generate the QR code
steps.body: Get the Outlook app opens a panel with a QR code that's generated fresh each time rather than a static one you could screenshot and reuse — a code that never expired would be a standing security risk if anyone saw your screen. Give the panel a moment; codes like this can take a few seconds longer to appear than a typical settings screen.

steps.heading: Scan it with the Outlook mobile app
steps.body: On your Android or iPhone, open the Outlook app and go to its account-adding screen — Settings > Accounts > Add Account > Email Account > Scan QR Code if you're adding this as an extra account rather than at first launch. Point the camera at the code on your computer and accept the pairing prompt. If it times out before you finish, refresh the panel in Settings to generate a new one.

troubleshooting.problem: There's no Mobile devices option, or no QR code appears, on a work or school account
troubleshooting.cause: Microsoft paused the QR sign-in rollout indefinitely for Microsoft 365 work and school accounts starting in September 2024. It's a deliberate rollback rather than something broken on your account.
troubleshooting.fix: Add the account with your email address and password instead, or check with your IT admin — some organizations control sign-in options through Microsoft Entra authentication policies and can re-enable it.

troubleshooting.problem: The phone camera won't scan the code
troubleshooting.cause: Outlook mobile doesn't have camera permission, or screen glare and low brightness are breaking up the code.
troubleshooting.fix: Grant camera access in your phone's app permissions and raise your monitor's brightness before rescanning.

faq.question: Does the QR code expire?
faq.answer: Yes. It's generated fresh each time and is time-limited. If the pairing sequence times out before you finish scanning, refresh the panel in Settings for a new one.

faq.question: Why is there no QR code option in my Outlook Settings?
faq.answer: If you're on a work or school (Microsoft 365) account, Microsoft paused this feature for that account type in September 2024. Personal accounts are less consistently affected, but the option can still be missing depending on your version of Outlook.

faq.question: Is this the same thing as Microsoft Authenticator or the 'approve sign-in' push notifications?
faq.answer: No. Those are a separate passwordless sign-in method, documented on its own by Microsoft, where Outlook mobile approves or denies a login attempt. This guide's QR code does something narrower: it adds the mailbox to the app so you don't type a password once.

faq.question: Do I need to touch any code to set this up?
faq.answer: No. Scanning the code and accepting the prompt is the entire process on both ends.

faq.question: What if my phone's camera won't scan the code?
faq.answer: Check that the Outlook app has camera permission and that your screen is bright enough for a clean scan — a dim or glare-heavy monitor is the most common cause of a failed scan.

verifiedNote: Click path and screens come from a recorded walkthrough. The Settings > Accounts > Mobile devices path and the 2024 pause for work/school accounts were cross-checked against Microsoft support and community sources in September 2026; Microsoft's own how-to article for this exact flow returned a generic support hub rather than readable content when fetched directly in this session, so that specific detail carries slightly less certainty than the rest. What is confirmed from a Microsoft page read in full is that the Outlook-mobile-as-authenticator sign-in method is a distinct feature from the QR code covered here, which is now called out explicitly in the FAQ.
